description: Goertzel single-bin DFT vs analytic magnitude. Three recurrences (K classic, alpha difference form for w near 0, beta sum form for w near pi) evaluated on a deterministic multi-tone signal whose bin magnitudes are known analytically: |X[k]| = N*A/2 for an integer-bin cosine of amplitude A (0<k<N/2). Cross-language invariants are accuracy, not timing.

entries.name: goertzel_vs_fft
entries.equations: x[n] = sum_i A_i*cos(2*pi*k_i*n/N + phi_i), n=0..N-1. K: s=x+c*s1-s2, c=2cos(w). alpha: d=d+x+(c-2)*s; s=s+d. beta: e=x+(c+2)*s-e; s=e-s. |X|^2 = sN^2 + s(N-1)^2 - c*sN*s(N-1).

magnitude.source: Analytic: orthogonality of integer-bin cosines gives |X[k_i]| = N*A_i/2. Calibrated at N=8192 in float64: observed max rel err 2.9e-11 (alpha and beta at k=1, from sqrt of a subtractive sum), 0 for K; rel_tol 1e-8 leaves >300x margin for libm cos differences across languages.

variant_spread.source: max over tones of |mag_alpha-mag_K|, |mag_beta-mag_K| relative to N*A/2; must be ~0 since all three recurrences realise the same filter.

entries.notes: Timing is not a cross-language invariant and is not checked. Octave, N=131072, interpreted for-loop: K 513 ms, alpha 488 ms, beta 490 ms vs FFT 1.0 ms (alpha/beta ~5% faster than K in the interpreter, not 23% slower). Fortran evaluator not implemented yet.
